title: Synchronous stdin writes can deadlock before timeout enforcement
reasoning: All stdin is written before communicate starts draining stdout and stderr or enforcing the timeout. Large input blocks indefinitely if the command does not read stdin. A command that produces enough output before consuming its input can also deadlock against the undrained output pipes.
reproduction: Execute a command that sleeps without reading stdin, provide input larger than pipe capacity, and set timeout=1. Execution can remain blocked in pipe.write beyond the timeout.
recommendation: Pass encoded input to communicate so input delivery and output draining run together under the timeout, and ensure exceptional paths terminate and reap the execution.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The stdin test sends a short string to cat; the timeout test supplies no stdin.
suggestedRegressionTest: Expand stdin coverage to large input, commands that do not consume input, and simultaneous large output, asserting bounded timeout and cleanup.
minimumFixScope: DockerExecRuntime stdin handling and execute lifecycle.

history.reasoning: Both evidence files exist, but the implementation changed: _write_stdin was replaced by _encode_stdin at exec.py:233–236, and execute now passes input directly to communicate with timeout at lines 304–307. Timeout and finally paths kill/reap the client and invoke container removal. The original stdin test moved to line 643; a communicate contract test exists at lines 526–557. Targeted validation of the current methods with real subprocess pipes passed: 4 MiB input to a nonreader timed out in 1.00s; simultaneous large output before input consumption completed in 0.05s. Client reaping and cleanup invocation were verified; actual Docker container removal was not exercised. An initial heredoc invocation was blocked by read-only restrictions; the equivalent in-memory invocation passed. No linked patch attempts were supplied.
commands: .venv/bin/python -B -c '<in-memory harness loading current execute and _encode_stdin via AST; real subprocess tests for 4 MiB unread stdin with timeout=1 and large stdout/stderr before input consumption; assertions for timing, output, reaping, and cleanup invocation>'
